judgment.regime_call: Lean risk-off: a strong tape on a hostile discount rate
judgment.summary: The economy is hot and the Fed is hiking into it. The 16 September hike to 3.75-4.00% was the first since 2023; the dots add one more, and the 2y at 4.85% (+61bp in a month, R_FED_PATH +97bp over fed funds) prices a cycle. The discount rate has broken out: 10y 5.11% (99.7th percentile of 20 years, +41bp in a month), 30y 5.40%, real 10y 2.76%, term premium up 21bp in three months, MOVE jumping to about 105. Stocks and bonds are falling together (60-day correlation +0.48), so Treasuries are not a hedge. The risk premium has not moved: HY OAS 273bp, VIX 15.7 in contango, NFCI loose, and the S&P 500 is 1% from its high. Earnings are carrying the index (Q3 EPS growth about +29%, GDPNow 5.1%, flash PMI 58.4), but the leadership is narrow: RSP -4.8pp and IWM -9.8pp against SPY over three months, and 5 of 11 sectors below their 200d. The cracks sit where rates bite first: housing (mortgage 7.03%, ITB -18pp in three months, NAHB 32), the CCC tail (the CCC-HY gap is at its 5-year high, +132bp in three months) and private credit (a record 6.3% default rate per Fitch). An oil shock (WTI +32% in three months, Brent about $107 on the Houthi strike on Yanbu) removes the Fed's room to look through inflation. This is the 1994 and 2018-Q4 setup, a Fed tightening into strength while the long end reprices. The index can hold up while earnings outrun rates, but the equity risk premium is about 1.7% over real yields and negative over nominal ones. Returns from here depend on earnings beating, not on the multiple, and the downside if the long end keeps going is a multiple compression like Q4 2018 (-20%).

positioning: Risk budget: 60% gross (mandate medium-low risk, Lean risk-off). Keep the rest in T-bills yielding about 3.9%, not long Treasuries, because the stock-bond correlation is positive
Cap long-duration growth at 15% of the book. Pre-profit space, quantum, nuclear and neocloud baskets are already lagging with breadth below 45%; do not average down before the 10y turns

Own earnings momentum with free cash flow: Mag 7 (accelerating, led by META), cybersecurity (accelerating, 100% breadth) and cloud leaders. Trail stops, because a +40pp run in three months into a 5% 10y is fragile
Energy as the oil-shock hedge (fit +0.9). Hold it while the Hormuz disruption is live; cut it on a ceasefire road map that reopens the strait
Semis and memory are improving over one month after a 3-month drawdown, and the allowlist is heating on MU, NVDA and SNDK. Add on confirmation at Micron's 30 September print, not ahead of it
Avoid homebuilders and housing-linked names, regional banks and levered small caps until the mortgage spread and MOVE fall together
Equity vol is cheap against bond vol (VIX about 16, MOVE about 105). Index put spreads are a better hedge than duration

what_changes_my_mind: Upgrade to Neutral or Lean risk-on: the 10y back below 4.75% with the MOVE under 90. Watch the 7-8 October 10y/30y auctions and the 4 November refunding statement. Then add duration: builders, long-duration growth, small caps
Downgrade to Risk-off and cut gross to 40%: HY OAS +75bp in a month (CREDIT_BREAK), VIX above VIX3M, or USD/JPY down 5% in a month (carry unwind as the BoJ hikes; next BoJ 29-30 October)
Further hawkish repricing: 14 October CPI with core at +0.4% m/m or more, plus a hike on 28 October. Cut the long-duration cap to 10%
Oil relief: Iran accepts the 60-day ceasefire road map and Hormuz reopens. Exit the energy overweight; the inflation pillar improves and the curve bull-flattens
Growth scare: 2 October payrolls negative and claims above 240k. Rotate toward defensives and duration; the bull steepener becomes the recession tell
